俸.title: salary; stipend
俸.reason: 棒 shares the visible 奉-like right side but has 木, and its complete lexical family covers rod/stick, line/dash and monotone speech, not salary. 借 and 付 share 亻 but name borrowing/renting and attachment. The actual current character articles were read. Neither money-related borrowing nor employment-related attachment makes the target mean those actions.
俸.rejected: 給 pay/bestow and 払 pay are not safe salary/pay distractors. No absent 奉 card is referenced. Three curated choices avoid default four-choice fallback.
俸.legacyFallback: Eleven current cards have fewer than three distractors: 人/休/何/入/出/口/女/日/月/男/買. Their actual displayed labels do not name salary/stipend; worker/person and purchasing/payment associations are not general synonymy. No change justified. Larger/random/live pools unverified.

pairDecisions.disposition: Direct salary/pay overlap in complete frozen families and actual current labels/bodies. Different public/private associations do not make competing salary answers safe. Each direct guard is on the new word; no transitive assumption.

Conservative direct salary/income label guards. A salary can be monthly and can be income, although neither general 俸給 nor 収入 fixes a monthly basis, and not all income is salary. Existing 月給 exclusions do not protect these new pairs transitively.

Conservative direct broad payment/provision-label safeguards: actual current labels mention payment or provision, and source families permit payment. This is not a teaching claim that the Japanese words are interchangeable: 俸給 names remuneration, 支給 its provision, 支払 a payment, and 代金 an amount owed in exchange. Guard the underspecified English labels rather than manufacture absolute compartments.

Both actual displayed labels are bare pay, which can be interpreted as the English noun in an uncontextualized choice even though the Japanese words are verbs. Exact-title deduplication between these two does not protect 俸給/pay. Add each direct pair without changing the existing teaching.

No new guard: fees/fare charged for use, personal spending allowance, a salaried employee and the receipt action are not names for salary in the inspected actual articles. Shared money/work topics are not by themselves reason for an exclusion clique. Whole-pool semantic certification is not claimed.

wordQuizAudit.limits: Direct conservative label guards, not legal payroll definitions, unrestricted substitution or proof of every random/live quiz's uniqueness.

Complete 払う and 支払う families retain financial and other senses, rare 掃う and search-only 仕払う separately. Their actual titles pay are ambiguous English labels next to salary/pay; no new reading, spelling, ateji or frequency lesson is added.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Proposed single necessary support: 俸給 ほうきゅう, salary/pay, especially public employees. Direct ホウ + キュウ provides a clear reading example. Preserve the broader employee use established by the actual Japanese entry. New word level remains unassigned unless independently sourced.

年俸 ねんぽう and 年俸制 ねんぽうせい are annual-pay comparisons, not mandatory new support articles. 年棒 is marked irregular kanji usage, not the preferred teaching spelling. Explain the compound's ポウ without inventing a raw ポウ metadata entry or pronouncing it ねんぼう. Annual basis does not imply a single annual transfer.

減俸 げんぽう salary reduction, 本俸 ほんぽう basic salary and 月俸 げっぽう monthly salary are valid secondary examples. No article is required merely to display the full family. Do not infer use frequency or legal payroll definitions from the entries.

Other salary/allowance families, standalone 俸, salaried-worker and raise/cut compounds remain source navigation. No manufactured everyday standalone use, register claim from missing flags, or extra vocabulary expansion.

Keep historical 俸禄 and rice-payment 俸禄米 distinct from modern salary, and archaic 食俸 distinct from neutral current vocabulary. 俸祿 is outdated spelling; 俸祿米 is search-only. Those spelling flags do not automatically label the pronunciations rare. Do not promote historical rice stipends into a universal explanation of present salary.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Pay/income comparison families: 給与 has employment-pay and provision senses; 給料 is salary/wages; 月給 specifies a monthly basis; 収入 and 年収 are broader income; 賃金 has rare spelling 賃銀 and rental-payment sense restricted to ちんきん; 報酬 is remuneration/reward. Compare actual displayed titles and ordinary meanings before choosing direct exclusions. Existing levels/readings/titles/exclusions stay unchanged.
Standalone 給 きゅう is explicitly a rare term. Its family is not evidence that the modern bound character is rare or that a standalone support article is needed.
代金 and 料金 concern payment due/charges; 料 has fee and material senses. Exact-spelling lookup also yields archaic 料 はやし under 栄/栄し; that is a different lexical identity and cannot support リョウ.

棒 ぼう is rod/stick, with line/dash and monotone Internet-slang senses. It is a useful shape contrast, not a salary synonym or a reason to pronounce 年俸 ねんぼう. Assess full target meanings before any curated wrong answer.
年 has separate とし, ねん and poetical とせ families. Annual-pay comparison uses ネン; do not attach とし or とせ to 年俸 or add an unnecessary new article.
人 person/suffix/counter families are separate lexical identities, not multiple readings of 俸. Explain radical 人 as visible 亻; historical morphology is not inferred from that radical.

付 has separate dated/effective づけ and attached/furnished-with つき/づき families, with kana-only katakana ツキ and luck sense qualifications. These are comparison evidence only; no allocation of those readings to 俸.
